title: Lena and the Asset
premise: Freya Dunmore, a fixer for an embassy that exists on no map, has spent seven years erasing problems for a government that denies employing her. When a voiceprint match unlocks a server in Tallinn, she discovers 'Lena'—the asset she was ordered to disappear years ago—is alive, and the files prove the embassy has been selling state secrets through its own fixers. Hunted by three governments and the assassin who once called her partner, Freya must smuggle the truth to a journalist before the embassy burns every witness, including herself. In the end, Freya trades her own invisibility—and nearly her life—to expose the operation, choosing truth over the only belonging she has ever known.
about_author: Freya Galloway is a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in postings she still cannot name. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Scottish Borders, where the nearest neighbor is a mile away and that suits her fine.

chapters.title: The Rules of Disappearing
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She cleans up a diplomat's scandal in Vienna with surgical efficiency, establishing her competence and the embassy's unspoken rules. A routine voiceprint verification pings an anomaly: a match to a dead woman. Emotional beat: controlled detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following the anomaly to a locked server in Tallinn, she finds files labeled LENA-ASSET—her own old case number—and discovers the woman she reported dead seven years ago is listed as active. Emotional beat: dread and disbelief.

chapters.title: What the Embassy Denies
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She confronts her handler, Marsh, who stonewalls and quietly revokes her access. That night her apartment is searched by professionals who left no trace but a single white glove. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she has become prey.

chapters.title: Lena
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In a safehouse outside Riga, Lena Voss—the asset everyone believes dead—works as a courier for the same network, unaware of what she carries. She notices her handlers watching her differently. Emotional beat: wary intuition.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Problem
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She pieces together that British, Estonian, and American intelligence all have claims on the Lena file—and all want it buried. A former colleague warns her to run, then is found drowned. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Craft
chapters.summary: Kaspar's POV. The embassy's assassin, Kaspar Rebane, receives the contract: Freya Dunmore. He studies her file and recognizes the tradecraft—it was partly his own teaching. Emotional beat: professional respect curdling into something like regret.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Using forged identities from her fixer days, Freya crosses into Estonia, evading border surveillance. She realizes every escape route she knows was designed by the people hunting her. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and defiance.

chapters.title: Two Ghosts Meet
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya tracks Lena to Riga; their first meeting is a knife-edge standoff in a tram depot until Lena sees the case number tattooed in Freya's file photo. Emotional beat: mutual recognition between two women erased by the same machine.

chapters.title: The Server
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena reveals the courier package she carries: an encrypted drive whose key is her own voiceprint. The files detail Operation GLASSHOUSE—state secrets laundered through deniable embassies for profit. Emotional beat: betrayal becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. In London, Marsh learns Freya has the drive and authorizes extreme measures, revealing his own complicity and fear of his superiors. He rewrites the rules one final time: no witnesses. Emotional beat: power corrupting a small man into a monster.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Hiding with Lena, Freya calculates odds, contacts, exits—and finds herself, for the first time, not alone. They plan to reach investigative journalist Ilse Brandt in Berlin. Emotional beat: fragile trust, the first taste of belonging.

chapters.title: Kaspar Closes
chapters.summary: Kaspar's POV. Kaspar corners them at a Vilnius rail yard; a brutal chase ends when he lets them slip—deliberately, he tells himself—because the file he was given omits why Lena was marked. Emotional beat: doubt infiltrating loyalty.

chapters.title: Berlin, Broken
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Their Berlin contact is compromised; Ilse Brandt refuses to meet without verification, and Freya must burn her last real identity to prove the story. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: The Price of Loyalty
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confesses she once informed on Freya's original team to survive—a confession that shatters their fragile bond just as Kaspar's surveillance tightens. Emotional beat: guilt, anger, and the question of whether loyalty can survive truth.

chapters.title: GLASSHOUSE Shatters
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Decrypted files reveal the final layer: the embassy plans to detonate a false-flag incident to bury the story and both women with it. Timeline collapses to seventy-two hours. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency.

chapters.title: Turned
chapters.summary: Kaspar's POV. Ordered to kill Lena publicly as part of the false flag, Kaspar instead delivers the embassy's internal kill list to Freya—an act of treason against his only employer. Emotional beat: loyalty inverted, conscience winning.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The trio races to move the drive to Brandt through a city filling with watchers. A decoy run fails; Marsh's teams take Lena. Emotional beat: desperation and resolve.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya offers herself in trade at the abandoned embassy annex where it all began, buying Lena's release while Brandt's team mirrors the drive live. Emotional beat: courage without guarantee.

chapters.title: Annex
chapters.summary: Climax, Freya's POV. Confrontation with Marsh; Kaspar turns his weapon on the embassy men; Freya forces Marsh to confess on record as servers mirror worldwide. Shots are fired; Kaspar takes a bullet shielding Freya. Emotional beat: catharsis amid chaos.

chapters.title: Front Pages
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. GLASSHOUSE breaks across three continents; governments scramble, denials collapse. Lena watches her own obituary get rewritten into testimony. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Kaspar survives, barely; Marsh faces inquiry; the embassy is dissolved on paper and reborn elsewhere. Freya testifies under her real name for the first time in seven years. Emotional beat: cost accounted, identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Lena and the Asset
chapters.summary: Dual POV epilogue. Months later, Freya and Lena meet in Tallinn—two women who chose truth over belonging and found each other instead. Neither is invisible anymore, and neither wants to be. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
